check.text: i was driving on the highway and the car started rocking violently back and forth.i applied on the brakes gently and the car started to slow down but would not stop shaking, almost causing the vehicle to flip over on its side. as this was happening my head was smashed against the side window multiple times, causing a concussion and cuts to my head and body. i was wearing my seatbelt at the time of the incident.when i came to a stop after nearly being hit by on coming cars i managed to pull the car over to the shoulder, while hitting the guard rail as i came to a stop. after i gathered my thoughts and when it was safe, i got out of the car to see what had happened and the rear control arm became completely severed from the frame due to excessive amounts of rust on the frame. i looked on the internet for similar issues and found that the toyota tundra, toyota sequoia, and various other toyota vehicles manufactured in the same year that share the same frame as my car had been recalled by

i have been driving since 1980 and have had various vehicles from various manufacturers and i have never had a dashboard melt for any reason. i expected my car to have minor problems at 40,000 miles but melting was not one of them. the interior of my car is melting. especially the glove compartment, the arm rest and the console. the glove compartment has melted and remain soft and sticky, to the point that anything coming into contact with the glove box leaves an impression or pock mar. the arm rest and center console have cracked and peeled. the drivers door handle came out in my hand as i was closing the door one day, that's when i realized it was made of 100 % plastic covered in vinyl. a car originally valued at $51k brand new and they install the cheapest door handle of any maker? they couldn't afford to put it together with screws, instead they glued it together. my glove compartment and dashboard is melting and sticky. it appears as though some type of glue had been poured on it.

i was driving about 35 mph on a rural road and i noticed that upon giving some gas the vehicle did not respond at all. then i noticed that all my instrument panel lights were out.everything gone. i applied the brakes and with difficulty in steering (there was no power), i pulled to stop at the side of the road. i then put the vehicle into park and turned the ignition key off, then restarted the vehicle and drove away. this is the only time this happened (last week).a complete loss of power. i know isuzu shares parts with gm (e.g. my transmission is gm). i hope this is not an example of that gm ignition switch problem.but certainly has the exact same symptoms of it. but it is very scary loosing complete power like that. *tr
